 Oral Order
1.

Accused Nos.1 to 4 are before this Court in this criminal petition filed under Section 528 of BNSS read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C., with a prayer to quash the entire proceeding in C.C.No.195/2024 pending before the Court of Civil Judge & JMFC Court, Maski, Raichur district, arising out of Crime No.33/2023 registered by Maski Police Station, Raichur, for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.
2. Heard the learned counsels for the parties.
3.

entities.text: Court of Civil Judge & JMFC Court, Maski, Raichur district
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 jointly submit that, the dispute between the parties has been amicably settled and the parties have filed an application before this Court under Section 320 of Cr.P.C., seeking permission from this NC:
2026:KHC-K:2041 HC-KAR Court for compounding the offences for which the charge- sheet has been filed against the petitioners.

They submit that, the dispute between the parties is amicably settled at the intervention of elders and well-wishers of both the parties and accused Nos.1 and 2 who are husband and wife, have decided to separate and live peacefully in future.
The parties who are present in person before this Court are identified by their respective counsels.
The application which is filed under Section 320 of Cr.P.C., is supported by an affidavit of accused No.1.
A separate joint memo is filed by the parties on 25.02.2026 reporting settlement and the said joint memo is also supported by an affidavit of the accused No.1.

The respondent No.2 has filed a separate affidavit on 25.02.2026 with a prayer to permit the parties to compound the offences for which charge-sheet has been filed in the present case against the petitioners.

In paragraph Nos.3 to 9 of the said affidavit, it is stated as follows:
(3) That I submit that myself, hence I am filing this affidavit to quash the entire criminal proceedings initiated by me against the petitioners, which is pending on the file of Hon'ble Civil Judge and JMFC NC: 2026:KHC-K:2041 HC-KAR Court at Noor Mohammed R vs The State Of Karnataka on 3 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64244106/
3 Maski, taluk Maski, district Raichur in C.C.No.195/2024 in the interest of justice and equity.
(4) That due to intervention of both the elders matter was amicably settled and the petitioners and respondent No.2 agreed the terms and conditions and intended to withdraw the cases pending against each other's i.e. C.C.No.195 of 2025 pending before Hon'ble Civil Judge and JMFC Court at Maski, Tq. Maski, Districit Raichur.

entities.text: JMFC Court at Maski, Tq. Maski, Districit Raichur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(5) That I submit that, I have filed maintenance case under Section 125 of Cr.P.C., in Crl.
Misc. No.1240/2023 against the petitioner No.1/accused No.1 pending before Hon'ble Civil Judge and JMFC at Lingasugur, taluk Lingasugur, district Raichur, against the petitioner No.1/accused No.1 and now the deponent as per the settlement deponent is ready to withdraw the case and take the permanent alimony from the petitioner No.1 herein/accused No.1 as a permanent alimony as full and final settlement of Rs.7,00,000/- (Seven lakhs) by way of Demand Draft D.D. bearing No.640861 of Canara Bank, Adarsh Nagar Branch, Kalaburagi-585105.
(6) That I further submits that, I have filed the FIR in Crime No.108/2023 on dated 14.08.2023 at Maski P.S., against the petitioner No.1/accused No.1 under Section 4 of "The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019", thereafter Interim NC: 2026:KHC-K:2041 HC-KAR order granted earlier is extended till next date of hearing.

District Raichur, against the Petitioner No.1/Accused No.1 which is pending before the Hon'ble Civil Judge and JMFC Court, at Maski, taluk Maski, District Raichur and as per the full and final settlement deponent is ready to withdraw the protest application.

sentences.text: (7) That, at the time of marriage, the petitioner No.1/accused No.1 is given the 20 gram of gold ornaments, 240 grams of silver chains as Maher (Dover) to deponent/me and thereafter as per the full and final settlement the Maher was not returnable to the petitioner No.1/accused No.1 and now the Maher (Dover) is on my custody which was not returnable to the petitioner No.1/accused No.1.

(8) That I am undertakes to withdraw all the Maintenance and Criminal cases which was filed against the Petitioner No.1/Accused No.1 and also I have no future claims as husband and wife and also I will not claim and maintenance or financial benefits or any other benefits from petitioner No.1/accused No.1 and I will never file any criminal and civil cases in future regarding the same set off facts against the petitioner No.1/accused No.1.

Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of D.P.Act, 1961, against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 4 which is pending on the file of the Hon'ble Civil Judge and JMFC Court, at Maski, taluk Maski, district Raichur.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 who is present before the Court has acknowledged the receipt of DD for a sum of Rs.7,00,000/- (Rupees seven lakhs only) from the accused No.1 towards permanent alimony in compliance of the terms in paragraph No.5 of the affidavit filed by respondent No.2.
5. The parties to this petition are all close relatives and the inter se dispute has been amicably settled at the intervention of the elders and well wishers of both the parties.
6. It is submitted that, the parties intend to give a quietus to their dispute and live peacefully in the future.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ramgopal and another Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in NC: 2026:KHC-K:2041 HC-KAR (2022) 14 SCC 531 has observed that, not withstanding the limitation provided under Section 320 of Cr.P.C., this Court in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., can quash the criminal case registered even for non- compoundable offences depending upon the gravity of the allegations, relationship between the parties and also nature of the settlement between the parties.

entities.text: Ramgopal and another Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, reported in NC: 2026:KHC-K:2041 HC-KAR (2022) 14 SCC 531
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the allegations against the accused are not of grave in nature and the parties who are all relatives have settled their dispute inter se and have decided to give a quietus to the same.
7. Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that, it is a fit case where this Court needs to exercise its inherent power so as to do complete justice to the parties who are before this Court.

8. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) The criminal petition is allowed;

NC: 2026:KHC-K:2041 HC-KAR (ii) The entire proceeding in C.C.No.195/2024 pending on the file of the Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Maski, Raichur, arising out of Crime No.33/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 498(A), 504, 506, 323 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961,
is quashed against the petitioners herein;
(iii) In view of the aforesaid order, I.A.No.1/2026 does not survive for consideration.

Sd/-
